III. 14. 6-11.] MAHÂVAGGA. 155

He spends that seven-day period within the residential boundary. For that monk, the first-period rains retreat is accounted for, and there is no offense for the promise. ||6|| But in this case... he departs having a seven-day obligation before the <term>pavâraṇâ</term> <gloss>invitation/conclusion of the rains retreat</gloss>. Whether that monk returns to that residence or not, for that monk, the first-period rains retreat is accounted for, and there is no offense for the promise. ||7|| But in this case, monks, a monk has promised a rains retreat for the first period. He goes to that residence and performs the <term>uposatha</term> <gloss>observance day</gloss>. On the following day, he approaches the monastery, prepares the sleeping quarters, sets out drinking and utility water, and cleans the grounds. He departs that same day having nothing to do. For that monk, the first-period rains retreat is not accounted for, and there is an offense of wrong-doing for the promise. ||8|| But in this case... [= § 8] ...he departs that same day having something to do—etc.—he stays for two or three days and departs having nothing to do—etc.—he stays for two or three days and departs having something to do—etc.—he stays for two or three days and departs with a seven-day obligation. He spends that seven-day period outside. For that monk, the first-period rains retreat is not accounted for, and there is an offense of wrong-doing for the promise. ||9|| He stays for two or three days and departs with a seven-day obligation. He spends that seven-day period within the residential boundary. For that monk, the first-period rains retreat is accounted for, and there is no offense for the promise. He... [= § 7] ...no offense. ||10|| But in this case, monks, a monk has promised a rains retreat for the latter period. While going to that residence, he performs the <term>uposatha</term> <gloss>observance day</gloss> outside. On the following day, he approaches the monastery, prepares the sleeping quarters, sets out drinking and utility water, and cleans the grounds. He departs that same day having nothing to do. For that monk, the latter-period rains retreat is not accounted for, and there is an offense of wrong-doing for the promise. But in this case... [the whole passage is identical with § 5-10; read instead of first-period and first-period promise: latter-period and latter-period promise, instead of before the invitation: before the <term>komudiyâ câtumâsiniyâ</term> <gloss>the full moon festival of the fourth month</gloss>] ...and there is no offense for the promise. ||11||14||

The Third Chapter on the Entering of the Rains.

Its summary:
To enter, when also, how many, and between the rains,
Those who do not wish, intentionally, to postpone, a lay follower.

<summary>This page details the specific legalities and disciplinary consequences for monks failing to fulfill their promised obligations during either the first or latter segments of the annual rains retreat.</summary>
